security_spec.violation_condition: OpenSBI M-mode code performs a memory access that straddles a PMP entry boundary, where the highest-priority matching PMP entry does not cover all bytes of the access. Per the clarified spec, the 'match all bytes' rule is evaluated before the privilege-mode/L-bit check—so even an M-mode access to an unlocked (L=0) region faults if it spans a partial PMP entry boundary (e.g., a doubleword load at a domain page edge where only half the access is covered by one PMP entry).
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: M-mode sd/ld/amoswap crossing PMP region boundary; sbi_domain_context save/restore with misaligned access near PMP edge; HSM suspend handler storing sbi_scratch to memory spanning PMP entry limit; M-mode memcpy/memset across PMP-configured domain ranges
security_spec.summary: PMP 'match all bytes' rule fires before the M-mode privilege bypass—OpenSBI M-mode handlers that dereference pointers near PMP region boundaries will raise access-fault exceptions even on unlocked regions, risking unrecoverable M-mode traps during domain context switches or HSM flows
